title: Meiosis: making sex cells
examples: What is the main difference between mitosis and meiosis?
Why is it important that sex cells have half the number of chromosomes?
How does meiosis help create genetic variety?

explain.say: Today we are learning about meiosis, which makes sex cells. These cells are called gametes. They are important for making new life.
The first thing to know is that meiosis halves the number of chromosomes. Normal body cells have a full set. Sex cells need only half that amount.
Meiosis involves two rounds of cell division. This process results in four new cells from one starting cell. These four cells are genetically unique.

draw.text: Four Cells: One Starts, Four Finish

explain.say: A key outcome of meiosis is genetic variation. This means the sex cells are not exact copies of the parent. They are slightly different.
In real life, when sperm and egg cells join, they combine their unique halves. This creates a new organism with the correct full set of chromosomes.
A common mistake is thinking meiosis is just like simple cell division. Remember, meiosis specifically reduces the chromosome number by half. This is its main job.

faq.q: Why do sex cells have half the chromosomes?
faq.a: They have half because when they join during fertilisation, the two halves combine to make a full set for the new organism. This prevents the new organism from having too many chromosomes.
asks: Why is the number cut in half?
What happens if the cells are not halved?

faq.q: What is the difference between mitosis and meiosis?
faq.a: Mitosis makes body cells that are exact copies for growth. Meiosis makes sex cells that are half the number of chromosomes.
asks: Which one is for making tissues?

faq.a: Variation happens because chromosomes can swap pieces between homologous pairs. This mixing creates unique combinations in the resulting sex cells.
asks: Does it make us different from our parents?

faq.q: What are the resulting cells called?
faq.a: The resulting cells from meiosis are called gametes. These are the sex cells that participate in reproduction.
asks: What are the sex cells called?

faq.q: Does every meiotic division result in different cells?
faq.a: Yes, due to the mixing of chromosomes, each of the four cells produced is genetically unique. This is the source of variety.

facts: Meiosis is a type of cell division used to produce gametes.
It reduces the chromosome number by half, from diploid to haploid.
The process results in four daughter cells from one original cell.
Genetic variation is created through chromosome mixing.

quiz.say: If a normal body cell has 46 chromosomes, how many will the resulting sex cells have?
quiz.why: Meiosis halves the chromosome number, so 46 divided by two equals 23.

wrong.0: This is wrong because it incorrectly doubles the number of chromosomes.
wrong.1: This is wrong because it suggests a simple division by two that ignores the biological process.
wrong.3: This is wrong because it describes mitosis, which keeps the full number.

quiz.say: What is the main purpose of meiosis in an organism?

options.show: To produce sex cells with half the chromosomes.
options.say: To produce sex cells with half the chromosomes.

options.show: To increase the total number of chromosomes.
options.say: To increase the total number of chromosomes.

options.show: To create identical copies for growth.
options.say: To create identical copies for growth.

quiz.why: This half-number ensures that when two sex cells combine, the offspring has the correct full set.

wrong.1: This is the main job of mitosis, not meiosis.
wrong.2: Meiosis always reduces the chromosome count, it does not increase it.
wrong.3: Creating identical copies is the role of mitosis.

quiz.say: When chromosomes swap pieces, what biological concept is demonstrated?
quiz.why: The swapping of genetic material creates unique combinations, which is called variation.

wrong.0: Replication is making copies; swapping is mixing pieces.
wrong.1: This describes a different type of cell division entirely.
wrong.3: While chromosome number is maintained after fertilization, the swapping itself causes variation.
